source.title: Latent Space Translation via Semantic Alignment
source.authors: Valentino Maiorca; Luca Moschella; Antonio Norelli; Marco Fumero; Francesco Locatello; E. Rodolà

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures whether simple transformations estimated from corresponding anchors can align representations well enough for zero-shot stitching; it uses a different method and task-based measures from the original sources.
record.gate_note: Rows capture the paper's reported translation and stitching outcomes bearing on whether representations can be mapped between models. The paper also cites similarity findings from prior work; those cited results are not recorded as rows. Figure 5 has no legible numerical values in the supplied text, so the cross-modal result is recorded only as the paper's explicit qualitative statement.
record.test_reason: The study fits affine, linear and orthogonal maps from parallel anchors between frozen encoders of different architectures, modalities and seeds. It then measures zero-shot stitching accuracy and latent cosine similarity, which bears directly on V4 (simple maps between models lose little). The same-architecture, different-seed autoencoder experiment also bears on V3: raw cosine is low but becomes high after a linear or orthogonal map.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also state that translation outperforms relative representations, and that pre-trained classification encoders are related mostly by near-orthogonal transforms. Autoencoder latent spaces, by contrast, are related by a class larger than orthogonal. They also say the best transform class depends on the task.
record.recipe_differences: Directly fits affine, linear, or orthogonal transformations from corresponding anchors and applies them to absolute latent spaces and existing decoders; unlike relative representations, it does not require a decoder trained on the shared relative space.
record.method_sensitivity: Transformation class affects results; affine/ortho generally perform well, while linear or l-ortho can drop on some datasets. Standard scaling versus L2 normalization changes results, with the authors noting stronger reliance of text encodings on norm information. Anchor quantity is examined in figures, but no numerical values are extractable from the supplied text.
record.problems: The principal cross-architecture table reports aggregate scores over encoder-decoder combinations rather than per-model results. Cross-modal Figure 5 values are not extractable from the supplied text. Reported experiments use corresponding anchors, so they do not establish mapping without paired data. The paper does not test scaling with model capability.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 results for non-affine transformations and vision datasets are omitted; Table 1 absolute and relative baselines are not repeated as separate rows. Table 3 latent MSE and reconstruction MSE, Table 4, Tables 5–6, Table 8, and figures with results are omitted because the retained rows already cover the reported mapping outcomes and the 60-row cap prioritizes primary results and observed partial outcomes.

untested.parts: No sweep over model scale or capability.
Cross-modal stitching is tested, but not whether alignment grows as the vision and language models improve.
Only one pair of seeds per dataset, small CNN autoencoders only; no unit- or feature-level matching.
Mapping without paired data, trained stitching layers, and relative representations as the decoder space (used only as a baseline) are not tested.
No interpretable features, neurons or circuits.
No comparison of similarity metrics, neighbour settings or out-of-distribution inputs.
No test of a plateau or of causes such as shared data.

missing.what: Table 2 linear and l-ortho results under L2 normalisation show larger drops (e.g. TREC linear 0.44, DBpedia linear 0.44 vs 0.78), so mapping quality depends on the normalisation choice.
Cross-bottleneck autoencoder stitching (250 vs 500 dimensions): affine lcos 0.95–0.98 but linear only 0.64–0.78.
Autoencoder stitching with L2-normalised decoders reaches lcos 0.96–0.99 for affine, linear and ortho maps.
Stitching results with MLP classification heads, including TREC no-stitch 0.41.
Numeric cross-modal stitching values for N24News are not readable in the text.

record.verdict_notes: The cross-architecture tables average over encoder pairs, so per-model failures are hidden behind large standard deviations (up to ±0.25). The 'absolute' baseline excludes pairs with mismatched dimensions. For the V4 rows, the comparison against no-stitch accuracy is the relevant baseline.

versions.untested_parts: No model scale or capability sweep, and no test of whether alignment rises with size or capability.
The paper tests cross-modal stitching on paired news text and images, but does not test whether alignment increases as both modalities' models improve.
The autoencoder experiment uses two runs with different seeds, but measures translation and stitching after fitting a map, not whether the networks independently learn shared features or subspaces.
Tests translation estimated from corresponding anchors and stitching with absolute decoders; does not test mapping without paired data or stitching layers.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are identified.
Compares transformation classes and normalization choices, but does not test convergence across similarity measures, neighbour settings, or out-of-distribution inputs.
Does not test whether alignment plateaus or whether shared training data or objectives explain it.

relationships.condition: Affine or orthogonal maps across pre-trained vision and text encoders, autoencoders differing by seed, and N24News text-to-image stitching
relationships.reason: Affine and ortho maps stay within about 0.05 of no-stitch accuracy on most datasets, versus near-chance absolute stitching (r1, r3, r4, r8, r12, r13, r16, r17, r20, r21, r33–r36, r54, r57). Autoencoder lcos rises from 0.09–0.34 to 0.78–0.96 (r37–r52). The authors report cross-modal improvement (r53, text only).
relationships.display_finding: Mapped accuracy stayed within about 0.05 of unstiched accuracy on most datasets versus near-chance absolute stitching, autoencoder lcos rose from 0.09–0.34 to 0.78–0.96, and cross-modal stitching improved.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Affine or orthogonal maps across pre-trained vision and text encoders, autoencoders differing by seed, and N24News text-to-image stitching
source_check.reason: Table 1 shows small losses in the successful classification settings; Table 3 and Section 4.3 report effective autoencoder translation and reconstruction. Section 4.2 explicitly reports improved image-classifier performance using translated text encodings.

relationships.condition: Linear or l-ortho maps, fine-grained CIFAR100, and text datasets (TREC, AG News, DBpedia)
relationships.reason: Loss depends on the transform class and the task: TREC l-ortho 0.57 vs 0.87 (r23), DBpedia l-ortho 0.57 vs 0.78 (r31), CIFAR100-F linear 0.62 vs 0.76 (r10). Other partial drops of 0.07–0.16 appear in r2, r5–r7, r9, r11, r14, r15, r18, r19, r22, r24–r30, r32, r55, r56.
relationships.display_finding: Performance fell to 0.57 versus 0.87 on TREC, 0.57 versus 0.78 on DBpedia, and 0.62 versus 0.76 on fine-grained CIFAR100, with other losses of 0.07–0.16.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Linear or l-ortho maps, fine-grained CIFAR100, and text datasets (TREC, AG News, DBpedia)
source_check.reason: Table 1 confirms task- and transformation-dependent losses: TREC l-ortho 0.57 versus 0.87, DBpedia l-ortho 0.57 versus 0.78, and CIFAR100-F linear 0.62 versus 0.76. These qualify the little-loss claim.

relationships.condition: Two identical CNN autoencoders differing only in seed and data shuffling, on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR10 and CIFAR100
relationships.reason: Raw latent cosine is low (0.09–0.34), so the bases differ, but after a linear or orthogonal map lcos is 0.90–0.96 (r37–r52), indicating a shared subspace.
relationships.display_finding: Latent cosine similarity rose from 0.09–0.34 before alignment to 0.90–0.96 after linear or orthogonal mapping.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Two identical CNN autoencoders differing only in seed and data shuffling, on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR10 and CIFAR100
source_check.reason: Section 4.3 establishes the seed-controlled setting, and r37–r52 show strong alignment after mapping despite low absolute cosine. The supplied rationale's range needs correction: linear and ortho yield 0.90–0.94; 0.96 belongs to affine.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: Affine or orthogonal maps across pre-trained vision and text encoders, autoencoders differing by seed, and N24News text-to-image stitching
labels.reason: Table 1 shows small losses in the successful classification settings; Table 3 and Section 4.3 report effective autoencoder translation and reconstruction. Section 4.2 explicitly reports improved image-classifier performance using translated text encodings.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: Linear or l-ortho maps, fine-grained CIFAR100, and text datasets (TREC, AG News, DBpedia)
labels.reason: Table 1 confirms task- and transformation-dependent losses: TREC l-ortho 0.57 versus 0.87, DBpedia l-ortho 0.57 versus 0.78, and CIFAR100-F linear 0.62 versus 0.76. These qualify the little-loss claim.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: Two identical CNN autoencoders differing only in seed and data shuffling, on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR10 and CIFAR100
labels.reason: Section 4.3 establishes the seed-controlled setting, and r37–r52 show strong alignment after mapping despite low absolute cosine. The supplied rationale's range needs correction: linear and ortho yield 0.90–0.94; 0.96 belongs to affine.

relation.reason: The study measures latent alignment and stitching performance between independently trained models, directly testing representational compatibility.

tranche.reason: Direct transformations between absolute latent spaces and evaluation with existing decoders test V4 using a different method from relative representations; the seed-controlled autoencoder experiments also bear on V3.

source_check.notes: Table 3 uses 1000 paired anchors, 500-dimensional spaces, standard scaling, and no additional decoder normalization. Its cosine values measure alignment after fitting a transformation, not a fraction of identical individual features.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Cross-architecture classification, same-architecture autoencoder translation, and the reported N24News text-to-image-classifier transfer
reader_labels.reason: Anchor-estimated maps produce strong classification scores relative to no-stitch references across many datasets (r1–r4, r8, r13, r16–r17, r20–r21, r24, r28, r33–r36), raise latent cosine similarity well above the absolute baseline in the autoencoder experiment (r37–r52), and the paper explicitly reports improved cross-modal classification from translated text encodings (r53).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Some cross-architecture datasets and transformation choices
reader_labels.reason: The mapping's downstream performance is not uniformly close to the no-stitch reference; notably several fine-grained, language, and linear/l-ortho results have larger drops (r6–r7, r10–r11, r18–r19, r22–r23, r29–r32).
